channel.title: Market Pressure Map · Indian markets
channel.description: Daily news scored for its impact on Indian market sectors and the rupee, bonds, inflation and foreign flows.

item.title: Sensex jumps 2,009 points (2.6%) to 79,310.01 and Nifty 2.4% to 24,536.60, a sixth straight gain
item.description:
Investors added about ₹7 trillion in wealth; midcaps rose 1.87%. Sensex is up 8.27% in six sessions on the oil slide, West Asia hopes and the US election. Rally accelerating.

Why it matters: Lower oil and foreign buying have repriced Indian equities quickly; a sharp US tech sell-off overnight is the first test of the rally.

Market gauges: Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +3

Confidence: high · horizon: days

item.title: Foreign investors buy a net ₹14,975 crore; domestic funds sell ₹10,445 crore (provisional)
item.description:
Fifth straight day of foreign buying and the largest so far, taking November above ₹32,000 crore after October's ₹52,100 crore exit. Domestic funds keep booking profits. Reversal deepening.

Why it matters: Very large foreign inflows support large caps and the rupee; heavy domestic selling shows valuations are being tested.

Market gauges: Foreign investor flows +3, Rupee +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: Brent rebounds 3.88% to $98.29 on new tanker attacks after Wednesday's 8.7% plunge
item.description:
Back above $100 in Asia on Friday, but still heading for a 12% weekly drop. Hormuz flows remain under 60% of capacity. Easing trend interrupted.

Why it matters: Oil near $100 still eases India's import bill compared with October, but renewed attacks show the relief is fragile.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance −1, Inflation outlook −1

Confidence: high · horizon: days

item.title: 10-year G-Sec yield falls 2 bps to 7.17%, down 24 bps in November; rupee at over one-month high
item.description:
Lower crude and a firmer rupee drive the fall from 7.48% in late October. Easing continues.

Why it matters: Falling yields cut funding costs for the government, companies and home buyers and lift banks' bond portfolios.

Market gauges: Bond market (G-Secs) +2, Fiscal & trade balance +1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks

item.title: Rupee ends unchanged at 94.46 per dollar after intraday losses, near a one-month high
item.description:
A firm dollar offset lower crude and foreign inflows. Holds after gaining for two sessions. Steady.

Why it matters: A stable, firmer rupee keeps imported inflation in check; renewed oil gains could test it.

Market gauges: Rupee +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: Nasdaq plunges 5.52% and Dow 1,833 points in an AI and chip sell-off after the US election
item.description:
Worst day since April 2025, wiping about $2.5 trillion; the chip index fell 10.2%. Fears of brakes on the AI buildout. Reverses Wednesday's post-election rally. New.

Why it matters: A US tech rout can weigh on Indian IT services stocks and foreign risk appetite, testing the six-day Indian rally on Friday.

Market gauges: Equities (Nifty & Sensex) −1, Foreign investor flows −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: Iran says two tankers and a tugboat caught fire in Hormuz; four attacks logged in 96 hours
item.description:
One blaze was tied to a mine. Iran keeps exemptions for Indian, Chinese, Iraqi and Qatari ships while the US blockade continues. Attacks persisting.

Why it matters: Continuing attacks keep insurance and freight costs high even as Indian ships gain passage, limiting oil relief.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: US midterm results will not affect the India–US trade deal, reports say
item.description:
The president keeps tariff and war powers; oil and Russia sanctions remain the main risks for India. Ongoing talks.

Why it matters: Continuity in trade talks supports exporters' tariff outlook; the deal's timing still depends on unresolved farm and dairy issues.

Market gauges: Growth outlook +1

Confidence: low · horizon: months

item.title: IEA sees India's gas demand falling 2% in 2026 despite a 10% jump in LNG imports
item.description:
High prices and supply disruption suppress consumption even as imports rise. New outlook.

Why it matters: Weak gas demand at high prices hurts gas distributors and fertiliser makers' margins, and raises the import bill per unit used.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: months
